issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side can be negative: for example, with x=1 and sufficiently small positive eps it approaches log(2/pi)<0, whereas the absolute value on the left is nonnegative. Moreover, from the displayed definition, the difference quotient approaches -log(2 sin(x/2)), which near zero behaves as -log x, not +log x as required by the expression inside the absolute value. The analogous second finite-difference bound has the corresponding sign problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the finite-difference inequalities by correctly signed bounds with nonnegative error constants and recheck each later use; only the local O(1) endpoint estimates are needed downstream.
issues.overall_effect: The stated standard estimates used to pass from Clausen-function differences to logarithmic endpoint terms are unavailable as written, so all later asymptotic calculations invoking them lack their stated support.
issues.title: The Clausen finite-difference bounds have impossible signs
issues.why_classification: The defect is local and the source's later arguments require only routine corrected first-order estimates, so the rates and scope can be preserved without new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The interval (-eps, n eps+eps) is chiefly outside the only interval on which a29 proves g_w<=U. Thus that comparison cannot bound this integral by its endpoint value. In addition, the integrand is e^{-2U_k}=|2 sin((x-eps k)/2)|^{-2}e^{-2U}, so a bound on U alone cannot simply omit the varying cosecant factor. No monotonicity or separate product estimate controlling this entire support-side interval is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a uniform estimate for the integral over (-eps,n eps+eps), including the canceled-node behavior of U_k, strong enough to recover a43 and the exponential estimate used in a44.
issues.overall_effect: The upper integral estimate in a32, the claim that the discarded region is exponentially negligible, and the resulting sharp equispaced inverse-norm asymptotics are unsupported. Consequently the general main theorem in the regime handled by a47 and its Fourier corollaries are not established.
issues.title: The support-arc integral is bounded using a parabola valid only on the complementary gap
issues.why_classification: The missing estimate is a nontrivial global bound on a different interval from the one analyzed, and the source supplies no valid substitute. Without it, the sharp equality case and a full parameter regime of the central results are lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The disk is closed. By the definition of distance to the finite set S, it contains at least one nearest point of S, and hence mu_S assigns it positive mass, at least 1/(n+1) under the proof's empirical-measure convention. Therefore KS is not bounded below by mu of that disk as claimed, and the proof obtains no bound of dist(z_+,S)^alpha by a power of KS.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the closed-ball hypothesis and argument by an open-ball or slightly smaller-radius lower-mass condition for which the empirical measure is zero, and verify that the revised regularity hypothesis still gives the required distance bound.
issues.overall_effect: The lower estimate for the maximum Lagrange-polynomial norm in a50 fails, so the lower side of the asymptotic equality asserted in the general Vandermonde-like theorem a10 is unsupported.
issues.title: A closed nearest-node disk is incorrectly asserted to contain no empirical mass
issues.why_classification: A comparable theorem may survive after strengthening or modifying one regularity hypothesis, but this is more than algebraic correction because the current assumption only controls the closed disk at the exact nearest-node radius.
